title: Role of Heat Treatment Atmosphere on the Microstructure and Surface Morphology of DLP-Fabricated High-Entropy Alloy Components.

recollection.starting_material: High-entropy alloy components fabricated via digital light processing (DLP)
recollection.intervention: Heat treatment in various atmospheres (e.g., inert, reducing, or oxidizing)
recollection.structure: Modified microstructure and surface morphology of the alloy components
recollection.mechanism: Atmospheric conditions during heat treatment influence oxidation, grain growth, and phase stability
recollection.results: Likely quantitative results include changes in grain size, phase composition, and surface roughness, depending on the atmosphere used during heat treatment.

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies atmosphere-dependent heat treatment and resulting microstructural/surface changes, largely restating the title. It does not identify oxygen-rich air versus oxygen-deficient evacuation, the debinding/sintering schedule, carbon retention, oxide barriers, gas-driven cracking, or enhanced diffusion and bonding. No actual temperatures, compositions, strengths, or transition points are recalled.
